title: MEHMO SYNDROME
alt_titles: MENTAL RETARDATION, EPILEPTIC SEIZURES, HYPOGONADISM AND HYPOGENITALISM, MICROCEPHALY, AND OBESITY
MENTAL RETARDATION, X-LINKED, SYNDROMIC, BORCK TYPE

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that MEHMO syndrome (MEHMO) is caused by hemizygous mutation in the EIF2S3 gene (300161) on chromosome Xp22.

checks.claim: MEHMO syndrome is caused by hemizygous mutation in the EIF2S3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequence analysis indicated that all patients carried a hemizygous mutation in EIF2S3 located on chromosome X as the most likely disease-relevant change.
checks.explanation: The paper links MEHMO to hemizygous EIF2S3 mutations.

checks.claim: The EIF2S3 gene is located on chromosome Xp22.
checks.evidence_quote: a candidate region spanning 10.7 megabases on the short arm of the X chromosome (Xp22.11-p21.1; Figure S2A)
checks.explanation: EIF2S3 was found in the Xp22 candidate region.

paragraphs.text: MEHMO syndrome is an X-linked recessive intellectual developmental disorder in males. Its name comes from its main features: mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity. Affected males have severe developmental delay, and many die early in childhood. Some patients also have glucose dysregulation and pituitary hormone deficiencies.

checks.claim: MEHMO syndrome is an X-linked recessive intellectual developmental disorder in males.
checks.evidence_quote: Inheritance | X-linked recessive | AR | AR
checks.explanation: Table 3 gives X-linked recessive inheritance for EIF2S3/MEHMO, and the affected individuals are males.

checks.claim: The name MEHMO comes from the main features of the syndrome: mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity.
checks.evidence_quote: Clinical hallmarks are mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism, and -genitalism, microcephaly and obesity. Life expectancy of patients is less than two years. Based on the major clinical symptoms this condition is referred to by the acronym MEHMO.
checks.explanation: The abstract lists these features and says the acronym comes from them.

checks.claim: Males affected by MEHMO syndrome have severe developmental delay.
checks.evidence_quote: Two brothers are described with a severe syndrome of postnatal growth and mental retardation which includes extreme microcephaly
checks.explanation: The paper describes severe mental retardation in the two affected males.

checks.claim: Many males affected by MEHMO syndrome die early in childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: Life span | Few months, oldest patient alive at 18 y
checks.explanation: The paper does not say 'many die early' in words. Table 3 gives the life span as a few months, and Table 1 records deaths at 2 y, 7 mo, 2 mo, 10 mo and 12 mo.

checks.claim: Some patients with MEHMO syndrome have glucose dysregulation.
checks.evidence_quote: Moreover, three of the patients developed insulin-dependent diabetes in the first year of life.
checks.explanation: Diabetes is reported, and Table 1 also lists neonatal or episodic hypoglycaemia.

checks.claim: Some patients with MEHMO syndrome have pituitary hormone deficiencies.
checks.evidence_quote: Other Endocrinopathy | Panhypopituitarism | Partial hypopituitarism | Small thyroid (1/4) | − | Low GH levels (2/3)
checks.explanation: Table 1 lists panhypopituitarism, partial hypopituitarism and low GH levels.

paragraphs.text: Steinmuller et al. (1998) described a family in which several males in more than one generation had severe mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism with hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity. They named the condition with the acronym MEHMO. Some affected boys died in early childhood.

checks.claim: Steinmuller et al. (1998) described a family in which several males in more than one generation were affected.
checks.evidence_quote: Haplotype and two-point linkage analyses in a large three-generation family assign the disease locus to Xp21.1-p22.13
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a large three-generation family. It does not say that several males were affected across generations.

checks.claim: Affected males in the family described by Steinmuller et al. (1998) had severe mental retardation.
checks.evidence_quote: Clinical hallmarks are mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism, and -genitalism, microcephaly and obesity.
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions mental retardation but not its severity.

checks.claim: Affected males in the family described by Steinmuller et al. (1998) had epileptic seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: Clinical hallmarks are mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism, and -genitalism, microcephaly and obesity.
checks.explanation: The abstract lists epileptic seizures as a hallmark.

checks.claim: Affected males in the family described by Steinmuller et al. (1998) had hypogonadism with hypogenitalism.
checks.evidence_quote: Clinical hallmarks are mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism, and -genitalism, microcephaly and obesity.
checks.explanation: The abstract lists hypogonadism and hypogenitalism.

checks.claim: Affected males in the family described by Steinmuller et al. (1998) had microcephaly.
checks.evidence_quote: Clinical hallmarks are mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism, and -genitalism, microcephaly and obesity.
checks.explanation: The abstract lists microcephaly.

checks.claim: Affected males in the family described by Steinmuller et al. (1998) had obesity.
checks.evidence_quote: Clinical hallmarks are mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism, and -genitalism, microcephaly and obesity.
checks.explanation: The abstract lists obesity.

checks.claim: Steinmuller et al. (1998) named the condition with the acronym MEHMO.
checks.evidence_quote: Based on the major clinical symptoms this condition is referred to by the acronym MEHMO.
checks.explanation: The abstract names the condition MEHMO.

checks.claim: Some affected boys in the family described by Steinmuller et al. (1998) died in early childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: Life expectancy of patients is less than two years.
checks.explanation: A life expectancy under two years is consistent with deaths in early childhood.

paragraphs.text: Borck et al. (2012) reported a family in which males had X-linked syndromic intellectual disability with microcephaly, among other features.

checks.claim: Borck et al. (2012) reported a family in which males had X-linked syndromic intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: three male individuals were affected by an intellectual disability (ID) syndrome with apparent X-chromosomal inheritance (X-linked ID, XLID)
checks.explanation: Directly stated.

checks.claim: Affected males in the family reported by Borck et al. (2012) had microcephaly.
checks.evidence_quote: Clinical features included moderate-to-severe ID, microcephaly, short stature, and facial dysmorphic features
checks.explanation: Directly stated.

paragraphs.text: Moortgat et al. (2016) restudied the family originally reported by Steinmuller et al. (1998).

checks.claim: Moortgat et al. (2016) restudied the MEHMO family originally reported by Steinmuller et al. (1998).
checks.explanation: The abstract describes two unrelated families. It never mentions Steinmuller et al. (1998) or MEHMO, and does not say it restudied an earlier family.

paragraphs.text: MEHMO syndrome is inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern. Only males were affected, and the disease passed through unaffected carrier females, as seen in the family reported by Steinmuller et al. (1998).

checks.claim: MEHMO syndrome is inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: A previously unrecognised X-chromosomal mental retardation syndrome is described.
checks.explanation: The abstract says X-chromosomal but does not say the inheritance is recessive.

checks.claim: In the family reported by Steinmuller et al. (1998), only males were affected.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not say that only males were affected. This may be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: In the family reported by Steinmuller et al. (1998), MEHMO syndrome was transmitted through unaffected carrier females.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention carrier females or transmission through them.

paragraphs.text: In the original family, linkage analysis placed the MEHMO locus on the short arm of the X chromosome, in Xp22.

checks.claim: In the original MEHMO family, linkage analysis placed the MEHMO locus on the short arm of the X chromosome, in Xp22.
checks.evidence_quote: Haplotype and two-point linkage analyses in a large three-generation family assign the disease locus to Xp21.1-p22.13, to a region that is flanked by CYBB and DXS365.
checks.explanation: Linkage did place the locus on Xp, but the interval is Xp21.1-p22.13, which reaches into Xp21. It is not limited to Xp22.

paragraphs.text: In affected males of a family with X-linked syndromic intellectual disability, Borck et al. (2012) found a hemizygous missense mutation in the EIF2S3 gene, which encodes the gamma subunit of eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 (eIF2). The mutation was ile222-to-thr (I222T). Functional studies in yeast showed that it weakened the binding of eIF2-gamma to the eIF2-beta subunit. This disrupted the integrity of the eIF2 complex and impaired translation initiation.

checks.claim: Borck et al. (2012) found a hemizygous missense mutation in the EIF2S3 gene in affected males of a family with X-linked syndromic intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: Identification of a hemizygous EIF2S3 missense variant c.665T>C (p.Ile222Thr).
checks.explanation: The variant is hemizygous and cosegregated with the ID syndrome in affected males.

checks.claim: The EIF2S3 gene encodes the gamma subunit of eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 (eIF2).
checks.evidence_quote: a missense mutation in eIF2γ (encoded by EIF2S3), the core subunit of the heterotrimeric eIF2 complex
checks.explanation: Directly stated.

checks.claim: The EIF2S3 mutation found by Borck et al. (2012) was ile222-to-thr (I222T).
checks.evidence_quote: Capillary sequencing confirmed the c.665T>C (p.Ile222>Thr) mutation
checks.explanation: Directly stated.

checks.claim: Functional studies in yeast showed that the EIF2S3 I222T mutation weakened binding of eIF2-gamma to the eIF2-beta subunit.
checks.evidence_quote: Biochemical studies of human cells overexpressing the eIF2γ mutant and of yeast eIF2γ with the analogous mutation revealed a defect in binding the eIF2β subunit to eIF2γ.
checks.explanation: The yeast studies used the analogous V281T/V281K mutations, not I222T itself. I222T was tested directly in HeLa cells.

checks.claim: The EIF2S3 I222T mutation disrupted the integrity of the eIF2 complex.
checks.evidence_quote: the I222T mutation identified in the affected individuals disrupts eIF2 complex formation by specifically impairing the binding of eIF2β to human eIF2γ.
checks.explanation: Shown in human cells.

checks.claim: The EIF2S3 I222T mutation impaired translation initiation.
checks.evidence_quote: we conclude that the Val281 mutations in yeast eIF2γ, and by analogy the I222T mutation in human eIF2γ, impair eIF2 complex integrity leading to defects in translation initiation
checks.explanation: The paper concludes this by analogy with the yeast mutants.

paragraphs.text: In affected males of the original MEHMO family (Steinmuller et al., 1998), Moortgat et al. (2016) found a hemizygous frameshift mutation in the EIF2S3 gene near the C terminus of the protein (I465fs). Functional studies supported impaired eIF2 function.

checks.claim: Moortgat et al. (2016) found a hemizygous frameshift mutation in the EIF2S3 gene (I465fs) in affected males of the original MEHMO family reported by Steinmuller et al. (1998).
checks.evidence_quote: a frameshift mutation (c.1394_1397del p.(Ile465Serfs*4)) were identified in the EIF2S3 gene in the hemizygous state in affected patients
checks.explanation: The hemizygous I465fs frameshift in affected patients is confirmed. Its identity as the original Steinmuller MEHMO family is not stated in the abstract.

checks.claim: The EIF2S3 I465fs frameshift mutation is located near the C terminus of the protein.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not say where the mutation lies in the protein (C terminus).

checks.claim: Functional studies of the EIF2S3 I465fs mutation supported impaired eIF2 function.
checks.explanation: The only functional work in the abstract is a zebrafish eif2s3 knockdown that reproduced microcephaly and short stature. No study of the variant's effect on eIF2 function is described.

paragraphs.text: In affected males of a family with X-linked syndromic intellectual disability and microcephaly, Borck et al. (2012) found a hemizygous ile222-to-thr (I222T) mutation in the EIF2S3 gene. In yeast, the mutation impaired binding of eIF2-gamma to eIF2-beta and disrupted translation initiation.

checks.claim: Borck et al. (2012) found a hemizygous ile222-to-thr (I222T) mutation in the EIF2S3 gene in affected males of a family with X-linked syndromic intellectual disability and microcephaly.
checks.evidence_quote: Identification of a hemizygous EIF2S3 missense variant c.665T>C (p.Ile222Thr).
checks.explanation: The affected males had X-linked ID with microcephaly, and the mutation is hemizygous.

checks.claim: In yeast, the EIF2S3 I222T mutation impaired binding of eIF2-gamma to eIF2-beta.
checks.evidence_quote: In contrast, the eIF2γ-V281T mutation substantially impaired eIF2β binding (Figure 2D, lanes 5–6)
checks.explanation: In yeast the analogous V281T mutation was tested, not I222T. I222T impaired eIF2β binding in human HeLa cells.

checks.claim: In yeast, the EIF2S3 I222T mutation disrupted translation initiation.
checks.evidence_quote: we conclude that the Val281 mutations in yeast eIF2γ, and by analogy the I222T mutation in human eIF2γ, impair eIF2 complex integrity leading to defects in translation initiation
checks.explanation: The yeast experiments used the analogous V281T/V281K mutations. The effect of I222T is inferred by analogy.

paragraphs.text: In affected males of the original MEHMO family reported by Steinmuller et al. (1998), Moortgat et al. (2016) found a hemizygous frameshift mutation in the EIF2S3 gene (Ile465SerfsTer4).

checks.claim: Moortgat et al. (2016) found a hemizygous frameshift mutation in the EIF2S3 gene (Ile465SerfsTer4) in affected males of the original MEHMO family reported by Steinmuller et al. (1998).
checks.evidence_quote: a frameshift mutation (c.1394_1397del p.(Ile465Serfs*4)) were identified in the EIF2S3 gene in the hemizygous state in affected patients
checks.explanation: The variant and its hemizygous state are confirmed. The abstract does not link the family to Steinmuller et al. (1998) or MEHMO.
